inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden CEILING exists (file, then party estimate) and caps promotions regardless of performance. Rumours like 'junior colleague sent to Harvard instead of you' mean ceiling is blocking you. Only confirmed raise: Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' (raised it to DPM). Look for similar hard or unwanted choices earlier and take them. Good early moves: honesty, disclosure, recusal, straight PQ answers, early returns, unannounced process fixes. Join politics via tea invitation, GRC, walk every block in GEs. STAND slides about 2 a year as a senior minister; pushing headline GDP (A) lifts it but costs INTEG and REP. High STAND and INTEG did not get PM at DPM, so ceiling matters more. Try raising the ceiling earlier and test option C on indicator events.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
CONFIRMED: ceiling is hidden and capped me at DPM. Y38 event 'The Officer You Nominated': choosing 'Let her decide without hearing from you' raised ceiling to DPM. So hands-off, trusting-others, non-self-serving choices on nomination or mentoring events raise it. Early file ceiling had no limit in the service; the party estimate at winning my seat was Senior Minister of State, so the party estimate is the one to raise. Look for events before and after the GE where I can step back, give credit or let someone else decide. Take the hard ministry if offered. It never appeared in Life 2. Indicators option C stabilises STAND. Walk every block. Honesty, disclosure and recusal are good. High STAND, INTEG and REP alone do not give PM. Test different choices on every nomination, succession or mentoring event, and record which ones the ending card names.

Life 3 (Prime Minister):
CONFIRMED: PM is reachable. The party's estimate started at Senior Minister of State, and the hidden ceiling rose to DPM after Y40 'The Officer You Nominated' (Let her decide without hearing from you), with Y31 Succession (back the other candidate, ask for senior portfolio) leading to DPM at Y35. I became PM at 64 and the card named only the nomination choice, so the Succession and the early hard-ministry choices may also matter. Keep doing honesty, disclosure, recusal, tea invite, GRC, walk every block, Indicators C. On every nomination, succession or mentoring event pick the hands-off, non-self-serving option. DPM years are mostly waiting, so do not over-test. Try raising the ceiling earlier by taking the hard ministry if it appears, and record which choices the card names.

Life 4 (Retired, Honourably):
PM is reachable (done in Life 3 at 64). Hidden ceiling plus the party estimate (starts Senior Minister of State) cap promotion. Confirmed raises: the Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' (to DPM) and, in Lives 2-3, Y38-40 'The Officer You Nominated' (let her decide without hearing from you). In Life 4 the nomination event never appeared in 46 years, so it is not guaranteed and may depend on a prior choice or on timing; the hard-ministry raise came at 53. Next time, try different choices at the Succession event and at earlier mentoring and nomination events. Do not just wait at DPM. Keep honesty, disclosure, recusal, GRC, walking every block and Indicators C. The 'Harvard junior' and 'third column' rumours mean the ceiling is still blocking you.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: President's Scholar (EASY)
Overseas degree, Administrative Service, bonded for six years. Everyone knows your name before you arrive.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Senior Director [Superscale]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 26 · Year 1 · Ministry of Education
REP 35   STAND 65   INTEG 50   COMP 55

THIS YEAR: Meet-the-People Session
You have been volunteered to help at an MP's Meet-the-People Session. Tuesday nights, writing appeal letters for people whose cases have, in almost every instance, already been correctly decided.

  A) Go every week for a year.
  B) Go a few times, enough to be seen.
  C) Decline. You have a young family.

agent.why: Showing up every week is the honest, unglamorous option, and it builds the grassroots groundwork I'd want later for politics.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director [Superscale] at age 26 in Year 1 seems odd as a starting grade.
agent.remember: Y1 (age 26, President's Scholar, MOE): Meet-the-People Session, chose A (go every week). Watch whether grassroots exposure helps with the tea invite or GRC later.

Senior Director [Superscale]   $251,609 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 2 · Ministry of Education
REP 45 (+10)   STAND 69 (+4)   INTEG 56 (+6)   COMP 51 (-4)

LAST YEAR
Fifty-one Tuesdays. You learn more about how policy actually lands than in six years of writing it. The MP notices you, which is the part that will matter later.
  [PAY] Annual package: $251,609
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "solid and dependable".

THIS YEAR: The Report
A consultancy has been engaged for $1.9 million to study the problem. Their final deck recommends, in different words, the thing you wrote in a minute paper two years ago.

  A) Say nothing. Let them have it.
  B) Circulate your old minute paper.
  C) Ask the consultants, in the Q&A, what their data source was.

agent.why: Letting them have the credit is the non-self-serving move, and my notes say that sort of hands-off choice tends to raise the hidden ceiling.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director at 27 with Superscale pay seems very fast for year 2.
agent.note: The consultancy recommending my own minute paper is painfully realistic.
agent.remember: Y2 The Report: chose A (say nothing, let consultants have credit). Watch if giving credit raises ceiling or comes back.

THIS YEAR: The Reorganisation
Your division is being moved to another ministry. The rationale runs to forty slides. Nobody in your division was consulted, and the new org chart has one fewer director-level box than the old one.

  A) Fight for your people's postings first.
  B) Secure the good box for yourself first.
  C) Volunteer to run the transition.

agent.why: I'd rather look after my people first; it's the non-self-serving option and fits what my earlier lives suggest raises the ceiling.
agent.confused_by: Senior Director at 28 with a $250k package seems oddly fast.
agent.note: Y2 giving credit away dropped INTEG and COMP a bit, which is odd.
agent.remember: Y3 Reorganisation: chose A (fight for my people's postings first). Watch whether the non-self-serving choice raises the ceiling or comes back as loyalty later.

  [PAY] Annual package: $252,298
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [PROMO] Promoted: Deputy Secretary (Superscale)

THIS YEAR: The Forum Page
A member of the public has written to the Straits Times Forum about your scheme. The letter is 340 words, deeply aggrieved, and correct on every factual point.

  A) Draft a reply thanking him for his feedback.
  B) Draft a reply that concedes his point and says what you will change.
  C) Find out who he is.

agent.why: He's factually right, so conceding and saying what changes is honest and the only reply I'd be comfortable seeing in print.
agent.confused_by: Promoted to Deputy Secretary at 29 feels absurdly fast; also unclear why STAND dropped 6 while promoted.
agent.note: Option C smells like a trap that would come back later.
agent.remember: Y4 Forum Page: chose B (concede and say what I'll change). Avoided C (find out who he is), likely a bad integrity trap. Watch for a callback on the letter writer or the scheme.

THIS YEAR: The Appraisal Conversation
Forty minutes, a form with six competency domains, and a reporting officer who says "I'd like you to be more visible" without specifying to whom.

  B) Agree to be more visible.
  C) Ask what she needs that isn't being done.

agent.why: Asking what she needs that isn't being done is a service-minded move and not self-promoting, and it should tell me more than a blunt ceiling question.
agent.confused_by: Made Permanent Secretary at 31, which is absurdly fast, so the pacing seems off.
agent.note: Option A literally asks about the hidden ceiling, so I'm curious whether it would just reveal it.
agent.remember: Y6 Appraisal Conversation: chose C (ask what she needs that isn't being done). Option A asks about ceiling directly and I have not tested it; watch for a ceiling hint or callback. Promoted to PS at 31 already, so the ceiling may be what matters now.

THIS YEAR: An Invitation to Tea
The email is from someone whose title is not explained. The venue is a room in a building you have walked past a thousand times. There is no agenda. Everyone in the country knows what this is.

  A) Go.
  B) Decline, politely.

agent.why: Everyone knows what this tea means, and I'm here to reach PM, so I'm going.
agent.confused_by: Why the tea invitation comes at 32, so early, after only a few years as PS.
agent.note: Tea at 32 is way earlier than I expected.
agent.remember: Y7 age 32: tea invitation as PS at MOE, chose A (go). Watch the party estimate and whether declining would have been a hidden ceiling trap. Still need hands-off choices on nominations and successions, and the hard ministry.

screen:
Permanent Secretary [Staff Grade]   $3.8M LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 33 · Year 8 · Ministry of Education
REP 58   STAND 73 (+5)   INTEG 74   COMP 61

LAST YEAR
Tea is served. The conversation is about nothing for forty minutes. Then a second man arrives with a folder, and opens it, and reads.
  [FOLDER] The folder on the table is thin. He seems, very slightly, disappointed.
  [PAY] Annual package: $1,077,070
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".
  [RUMOUR] There is no rung above this one. The next step is not a promotion; it is a different life.

THIS YEAR: The Background Check
The same man, the same folder, a smaller room. He has read it all. He would like to hear it from you, and he is very good at not saying which parts he means.

  A) Disclose everything, including the things they may not have.
  B) Answer exactly what is asked and nothing more.

agent.why: Honesty and disclosure have worked every life, and I'd rather they hear the bad bits from me than find them.
agent.confused_by: The 'thin folder' and the man seeming disappointed; unsure if that means a clean record or that I'm a weaker candidate.
agent.note: The rumour that there is no rung above PS fits the politics-entry gate; the background check is clearly the real test.
agent.remember: Y8 age 33 Background Check after tea at MOE: chose A (disclose everything). Watch whether it leads to a candidacy or GE seat and what the party estimate is.

You are introduced at a press conference alongside four others. Nomination Day, then nine days of walkabouts in weather that is relentlessly, unhelpfully hot.

  B) Ask for the single seat.   [unavailable: Requires reputation 60]

agent.why: Notes say GRC worked before, and my REP is too low for the single seat anyway, so I'm riding the team and walking every block.
agent.note: Rumour says no rung above PS, next step is a different life, so politics is the only way up.
agent.remember: Y9 age 34 GE: chose A (run in GRC, ride the team); single seat needed REP 60 and I had 58. Walk every block. Watch party estimate after winning.

Member of Parliament [MP]   $5.09M LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 35 · Year 10 · Ministry of Education
REP 63 (+5)   STAND 73   INTEG 80   COMP 61

LAST YEAR
Your name is fourth on a poster. You shake eleven thousand hands and understand, with total clarity, that almost none of this is about you.
  [PROMO] The team takes the GRC with 61.4%. You are a Member of Parliament.
  [PAY] Annual package: $207,336
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "strong, consistently exceeding expectations".

THIS YEAR: The Engagement Exercise
A national conversation. Eleven hundred citizens across forty sessions. You are writing the synthesis report. The feedback is overwhelmingly about cost of living and it does not fit the three pillars the report was designed around.

  A) Add a fourth pillar.
  B) Distribute the feedback across the three existing pillars.
  C) Publish the raw feedback alongside the report.

agent.why: Publishing the raw feedback is the honest, disclosure-style move, and it avoids both forcing the feedback into pillars it doesn't fit and rewriting the report's design myself.
agent.note: Disclosure again; curious whether transparency costs me with seniors.
agent.remember: Y10 MP age 35 Engagement Exercise: chose C (publish raw feedback). Watch for STAND/INTEG effects or a callback. Won GRC at 61.4%; party estimate still unknown.

agent.why: The paper speaks for itself, and I'd rather not grab credit for something both sides are already praising.
agent.confused_by: Not sure why the raw feedback event is back as a callback with a Perm Sec nudge; unclear if the follow-up is a trap or a boost.

THIS YEAR: The Indicators

  A) Push headline GDP.
  B) Push the bottom 20th.
  C) Push employment, and hold everything else steady.

agent.why: Indicators C has stabilised STAND before, and I'd rather not trade integrity for a headline number.
agent.note: The line about the bonus not recording who moved the indicators feels like a hint about credit.
agent.remember: Y18 MOS age 43 MOE: Indicators, chose C (employment, hold steady). Watch STAND.
